incident-bot: :warning: INCIDENT ALERT — 1764501234 — Severity: S2. Degraded embeddings throughput observed across region us-west-2. Paging oncall: @alice.chen. Brief: sudden increase in per-request memory use, causing queuing and elevated latencies. Monitoring links: <https://ops.redwood/inci/1764501234>

alice.chen: taking this — grabbing context and logs now. @jordan.patel if you can shadow for infra changes?

jordan.patel: on it. I see elevated GPU memory usage in pool-rw-3 starting ~14:17 UTC, correlates with a spike in batched requests from one client. pulling kernel traces and nvml logs.

maria.gomez: looping in CS — I can draft a short customer note for affected tenants while you triage. anyone have a quick impact estimate?

jordan.patel: preliminary: ~12 customers saw >2x latency for embedding calls, 3 customers had request errors (5xx). no data exposure. severity S2 because customer-facing degradation.

sam.khan: engineering note: recent batching tweak (accumulate up to 512 tokens before dispatch) may be accumulating KV cache unexpectedly for long-context pipelines. quick mitigation: rollback accumulation limit to 256 to reduce peak memory. I can push a config rollback to the staging pool then prod after verification.

alice.chen: please do the rollback, @sam.khan. Jordan, can you confirm we won't regress throughput for small requests?

jordan.patel: I'll run a small A/B on two host groups. If rollback looks clean, we'll promote.

incident-bot: ACTIONS CREATED: #1764501234 -> handoff to alice.chen; mitigations: rollback-batching-256 (assigned to sam.khan) ; status-page-draft (assigned to alice.chen).

maria.gomez: status page draft (please review):
```
We are currently experiencing elevated latency and intermittent errors for embedding requests in us-west-2. Engineers are investigating and have deployed a temporary rollback to batching configuration to mitigate the issue. Impact: some customers may see slower responses or occasional 5xx errors. We will post updates as we have them. Incident ID: 1764501234.
```

liam.support: suggestion: call out "no data exposure" in the status page and give an ETA for next update (30m). otherwise looks good.

alice.chen: agreed. edit status page to include "no data exposure" and add ETA 30m. I'll post the page once Jordan confirms rollback is stable.

sam.khan: rolling back accumulation cap to 256 on pool-rw-3 now. command:
```
# rollback batching
redwoodctl configs set pool-rw-3 batching.accumulation_limit=256 --force
```

sam.khan: monitor: GPU mem usage falling back to baseline over 2 minutes, queues draining.

jordan.patel: seeing reduced queuing, error rates dropping. marking mitigation as successful.

alice.chen: posting status page update now. draft note posted to status.redwood.com/incidents/1764501234 — includes "no data exposure" and next update ETA +30m.

maria.gomez: customer notification draft (short form) — please review before we send to affected accounts:
```
Subject: Brief service degradation for embedding API (US-WEST-2) — Resolved

Hi —

We experienced a service degradation affecting embedding calls in the US-WEST-2 region earlier today (Incident 1764501234). Engineers identified a batching configuration change that caused elevated memory pressure and intermittent 5xx errors for some requests. We rolled back the batching accumulation limit and the service returned to normal.

What happened: configuration change caused memory accumulation in long-context pipelines.
What we did: rolled back batching accumulation limit to reduce memory pressure; monitors show error rates returned to baseline.
Impact: brief latency increase and intermittent errors for a subset of customers; no data exposure.
Next steps: full RCA and preventative actions to follow within 72 hours. If you saw issues we missed, please reply and we will prioritize follow-up.

Thanks,
Redwood Customer Success
```

liam.support: looks good. recommend not sending to the entire tenant list at once — stagger to the 3 customers who hit errors first, then wider notification after 1 hour if no regressions.

alice.chen: copy. @maria.gomez please send first-wave to the 3 affected customers within 15m. Sam/Jordan, can you create a short postmortem timeline I can include in the follow-up?

sam.khan: will prepare a short engineering timeline (root cause + rollback steps) and post here in the next 2 hours.

jordan.patel: adding monitoring rule to alert on accumulation_limit breaches and a runbook step to rollback automatically if error rate > 1% sustained for 5m. file: ops/playbooks/batching-accumulation.md (internal).

maria.gomez: sending first-wave now. tagging customers A,B,C and noting our support inbox for replies. :mailbox_with_mail:

alice.chen: thank you all. next actions: 1) Maria send customer notes (first-wave), 2) Sam/Jordan prepare RCA timeline and mitigation playbook, 3) Ops to add alert and automated rollback. I'll schedule an internal post-incident review and share the final customer-facing RCA within 72 hours.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1764501234 — MITIGATION APPLIED by sam.khan — status: monitoring.

maria.gomez: received a reply from Customer B asking for exact timestamps and whether any API retries are needed. I'll collect their logs and route to eng.

alice.chen: timeline clarification request: include exact start time of degradation (14:17 UTC) and time mitigation completed (14:31 UTC). Maria, include that in replies.

sam.khan: confirmed. adding to RCA notes: start=2026-02-03T14:17:12Z, mitigation=2026-02-03T14:31:08Z.

jordan.patel: filing follow-up task: ENG-176450-1 (add guardrail tests for new batching changes) assigned to sam.khan.

alice.chen: great. closing this thread for live mitigation — will reopen for RCA discussion. :white_check_mark:
